title: LinkedIn cofounder says AI infrastructure is the 'only reason we're not in a recession'
key_facts: Reid Hoffman, LinkedIn cofounder, said on the Newcomer podcast released Friday 2 Oct 2026 that capital behind the AI infrastructure buildout is 'the only reason we're not in a recession'.

He said most of that capital is distributed across the country rather than concentrated where data centers are built, and that it pays construction workers, electricians, carpenters, real estate agents and lawyers.
He said data center builders need to work fairly with local communities so both sides get a good deal.
Context from BI: data centers have become a bipartisan political issue before the midterms; Republican and Democratic governors have moved to curtail construction.
Pew Research Center poll (surveyed in August, released last week): half of rural Americans say data centers are mostly bad for the environment, up from 32% in January.
BI notes the broader economy is still growing: real GDP grew at a 2.2% annual rate in the second quarter, unemployment remains low despite a disappointing September jobs report.
quote_evidence: Hoffman credited the huge amount of capital behind the AI infrastructure buildout for being "the only reason we're not in a recession."
"Most of that's more distributed across the country," he said. "That's great."
Real gross domestic product grew at a 2.2% annual rate in the second quarter; that measure typically declines during recessions.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent tech investor argues the data center boom is propping up the US economy at the moment voters are turning against data centers.
notes: Podcast was released Friday 2 Oct, so the underlying remarks predate the 3 Oct window by a day. BI's own reporting; the recession claim is Hoffman's opinion, and BI's own figures show growth continuing.
